questions.q: Why should I respond to positive reviews?
questions.a: Replying to a positive review makes the guest feel appreciated and gives your brand a human voice. It's also free promotion, since other diners read your replies when deciding where to eat. A good reply can bring that guest back and help you reach new ones.

questions.q: What should a reply to a positive review include?
questions.a: Start by thanking the guest for taking the time to write, then mention something specific from their review and use their first name. Add a little value, such as suggesting a dish to try next time, and invite them back. Keep it short, warm and in your brand's voice.

questions.q: How do I avoid sounding generic when replying to good reviews?
questions.a: Skip copy-pasted lines like a plain thank you for your kind words, because guests can tell when a reply comes from a template. Refer to the dish, the staff member or the moment they mentioned, and address them by name. If you use templates to save time, keep a few versions and personalize each one.

questions.q: Can I offer a discount when replying to a positive review?
questions.a: Yes, a small offer such as a discount on the next visit or an invitation to your loyalty program is a friendly way to return the gesture. It gives the guest a concrete reason to come back. Keep the tone generous and low-key so the reply doesn't read like a sales pitch.

questions.q: How quickly should I respond to positive feedback?
questions.a: Respond as soon as you can, ideally while the visit is still fresh in the guest's mind. A quick reply shows you value what they said, while a late one carries much less impact. Setting up a library of customizable replies helps your team keep pace.
